page: Amazon Web Services r7a.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor with 4 dedicated physical cores operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance evaluations indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring in the top 25%. Geekbench text processing also demonstrates strong results. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth write speeds fall into the average tier. A notable performance bottleneck is observed in large-block, uncached read-only memory bandwidth, which registers in the bottom 25% at 37.49 GB/sec. Similarly, LLM inference speeds for medium 7B models are weak, processing 23.33 tokens per second for prompts and 8.53 tokens per second for text generation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r7a.xlarge offers a dense DDR5 memory allocation relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The absence of bundled local storage and low baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps are key architectural tradeoffs to consider. This instance is best suited for memory-intensive applications such as medium-sized databases, caching layers like Redis, text processing pipelines, and general-purpose workloads requiring high memory capacity per vCPU.
